summary: Same pattern and near-identical single-nova physics (birth rate, growth, decay, palette all match to within a few percent), but the original hard-kills novas mid-flight — producing dark gaps, flicker cuts and occasional full-strip blackouts — while the port lets every nova fade out smoothly, so it runs ~47% brighter and never goes dark.
observations: Rig/controls: strip, 60 px, no controls on EITHER side (probe: 'no settable controls' for orig and port) — control surfaces match, nothing to dial.

Both sides draw the same thing: bright ~4-6 px cores ('novas') that ignite at 255, then expand outward and dim, drawn as smooth bell-shaped bumps that are summed together on the strip. Waterfall reads as apex-up triangles widening downward.

Isolated first nova (t=0.00-1.20 s, 20 fps, seed 1) is essentially IDENTICAL: peak brightness decays 255->98 with the two sides agreeing to the unit at every 0.05 s sample (255/254, 174/176, 117/117, 98/98). Half-max width grows 4->14 px (orig) vs 5->16 px (port) — port ~10% wider. Centroid 32.5 (orig) vs 33.0 (port), a ~0.5 px offset that persists (index-centring convention).

Spawn rate matches: 58 brightness peaks in 60 s at 20 fps on BOTH sides (~1/s). Novas are spawned at nearly the same times and pixel positions on both sides for the first ~4.8 s of seed 1 (births at orig 0.00/1.25/2.00/2.70/3.35/4.35/4.45 vs port 0.00/1.30/1.85/2.75/3.25/4.40/4.50), so the RNG draw order lines up.

MAIN DIVERGENCE — abrupt nova death. In 60 s at 20 fps the original has 35 single-frame mean-brightness drops of >25% (e.g. 4.85 s 74->27, 12.40 s 50->9, 19.10 s 54->1, 36.90 s 54->2); the port has ZERO such drops. Per-pixel dumps confirm these are whole blobs vanishing in one frame (at 4.85 s two separate bumps, one only 0.4 s old, both go to exactly 0 while the rest of the profile is untouched). In the waterfall this is the sharp horizontal cut that truncates each of the original's cones.

Consequence 1 — full blackouts. Original goes ALL-ZERO on 22 of 1200 frames in 60 s, in 4 clusters (5.50 s x2 frames, 5.75 s x3, 10.75 s x9, 43.20 s x8 = 0.10-0.45 s of total darkness each). Port's floor never drops below mean brightness 13-15 and it never has a black frame in any run.

Consequence 2 — density/brightness. Mean brightness over 60 s: orig 36.7 vs port 55.0 (+50%); excluding the original's blackout frames it is still 37.4 vs 55.0 (+47%), so the blackouts are NOT the cause. Same offset in every window tried: 6 s baseline 36/45, 60 s survey 39/53, 240 s survey 35/47, late window (--skip 120, 30 s) 34/54, seed 7 34/46, seed 1234 34/47.

Consequence 3 — dark space. Over a 240-frame / 60 s dump scan, 35.3% of orig pixel samples are below 8/255 vs 19.5% for the port; median pixel value 20 (orig) vs 45 (port); median half-max feature width 12 px (orig) vs 16 px (port). Concurrent local maxima: orig avg 2.13 (15/240 frames with none at all) vs port avg 2.61 (never zero).

Peak-brightness distribution: orig has 23/240 sampled frames whose brightest pixel is under 32/255 (near-dark lulls) and 120 at full 255; port has 0 such lulls and 147 at 255. The original's 'quiet' stretches (max pixel 7-15 across the whole strip) have no counterpart in the port.

Colour matches well. Both sides use the same bimodal warm palette: hues clustered at ~8-18 deg (orange/tan) and ~343-352 deg (pink/magenta), whites at the cores. Mean saturation of the brightest pixel 0.263 (orig) vs 0.281 (port); max 0.61 vs 0.64. Channel means track the same R>G~=B ratio on both sides.

No modes/regimes. The 60 s / 5 fps survey and the 240 s / 2 fps extended survey both show one continuous stochastic regime on both sides — no palette walk, no long-period cycle, no mode rotation. Brightness autocorrelation over 1200 frames shows no periodic peak on either side (monotonic decay from lag 3), consistent with pure Poisson-ish spawning.

Steady state is fine on both sides: brightnessTrend 'steady' for orig and port over 60 s at 20 fps, and a --skip 120 / 30 s late window is statistically indistinguishable from the opening window on each side (orig 34/port 54). The port does not decay, freeze or saturate.

No frame-rate coupling on either side: mean brightness is fps-invariant at 10/20/40 fps (orig 38.8 / 36.7 / 39.4; port 54.3 / 55.0 / 56.5), so both engines drive the animation off elapsed time, not per-frame steps.
Original's zeroMotionFrames is 102/1200 (its blackout runs) vs port 1/1200 — that number is a symptom of the blackouts, not of a frozen side.

Seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 all show the same picture — original waterfall crossed by hard black horizontal cut lines with real dark gaps, port a continuous overlapping lattice with almost no black.

Re-rendered on an 8x8 grid rig (12 s, 20 fps) as a second lens: the rhythm images show the same split — the original's rhythm has full-width black bands where the port's is continuous, and the port is again brighter (mean 37 vs 56). No additional structural divergence appeared on the grid.
Neither side reports a compile or runtime error, and neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).
feedback: The single-nova model is already right — do not touch the growth or decay curves. An isolated nova matches the original to within a unit of 8-bit brightness over its first 1.2 s (255->98) and within 1-2 px of width. All the remaining error is in nova LIFETIME/retirement.

The port never retires a nova: its blobs decay asymptotically and keep contributing forever, so they accumulate. The original removes a nova INSTANTLY and completely — one frame it contributes a full bell curve, the next frame it contributes exactly 0. Add that hard retirement. Symptom to fix against: the original posts 35 single-frame >25% drops in mean brightness per 60 s; the port posts 0.

Retirement is not a simple fixed age. In the original, several novas can die in the SAME frame (at t=4.85 s a 0.4 s-old blob and a much older wide blob both vanish together), which looks like a bounded slot pool being reclaimed/recycled rather than each nova expiring on its own timer. Whatever mechanism is used, it must be able to kill a young nova and it must sometimes empty the pool entirely.

The original's pool does go completely empty: expect the strip to be fully black (all 60 pixels exactly 0) for 2-9 frames at 20 fps, about 4 times per minute. The port's mean brightness floor of 13-15 is the giveaway that this never happens; after the fix the floor should reach 0.

Target the density statistics, not just the look: over a 60 s window the original sits at mean brightness ~37 with ~35% of pixel samples below 8/255, median pixel 20, and ~2.1 concurrent blobs; the port is at ~55, 19.5%, median 45, ~2.6 concurrent. Fixing retirement should pull all four toward the original at once. Do NOT try to fix the brightness gap by dimming novas globally — per-nova peak brightness already matches exactly and dimming would break that.

The original also has visible 'quiet' stretches where the brightest pixel on the whole strip is only 7-15/255 (a single very old, very wide, very faint blob). The port has none of these; they should reappear once novas are retired and the pool is allowed to run low.

Minor: the port's blobs are consistently ~10% wider at the same age (half-max 5->16 px over 1.2 s vs the original's 4->14 px) and the whole figure sits ~0.5 px to the right (centroid 33.0 vs 32.5 for the same nova). Looks like an i vs i+0.5 pixel-centre convention plus a slightly larger width constant. Cosmetic — fix only after retirement.

Spawn rate, spawn positions, palette (two hue clusters at ~13 deg and ~347 deg), saturation and fps-invariance are all correct; no work needed there. Neither side has controls, so there is nothing to add or remove on the dial surface.
